title: You keep telling yourself you don’t have enough.
paragraphs: You keep telling yourself you don’t have enough.

Not enough strength.
Not enough confidence.
Not enough resources.
Not enough faith.
And you’ve quietly made that your excuse.
Gideon did the same thing.

When God called him, he wasn’t standing on a battlefield. He was hiding—literally threshing wheat in a winepress, trying not to be seen, trying to survive. Then the voice of God cut straight into his fear:
“The LORD is with you, mighty warrior.” (Judges 6:12)
That must have sounded almost offensive.
Because Gideon didn’t feel mighty. He felt small. Invisible. Disqualified.
And when God gave him the assignment—to save Israel—Gideon immediately pushed back:
“Please, Lord, how can I save Israel? My clan is the weakest… and I am the least in my family.” (Judges 6:15)
That’s your voice too.
You’ve rehearsed that speech. Different words, same meaning.

“I’m not ready.”
“I’m not called like others.”
“I don’t have what it takes.”
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God didn’t argue with Gideon’s weakness.
He ignored it.
“The LORD turned to him and said, ‘Go in the strength you have… Am I not sending you?’” (Judges 6:14)
Read that again.
Go in the strength you have.

Not the strength you wish you had.
Not the strength you’re waiting for.
Not the version of you that doesn’t exist yet.
The strength you have.
That means God already accounted for your limitations before He ever called you.
God saw it.

The fear.
The insecurity.
The past failures.
The hidden sin you thought disqualified you.
You knew.
And still… He called.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
This is where everything shifts.
Because the calling of God is not based on your capacity—it’s based on His presence.
“The LORD said to him, ‘I will be with you, and you will strike down all the Midianites.’” (Judges 6:16)
Not you will succeed because you’re strong.
But you will succeed because I am with you.
That’s the difference.

You’ve been trying to upgrade yourself enough for God to use you.
God is calling you as you are—and planning to transform you on the way.
But Gideon’s story doesn’t stay comfortable.
Because God starts stripping things away.
An army of 32,000? Reduced to 300.
Why?
“So that Israel may not boast against me that her own strength has saved her.” (Judges 7:2)
God will intentionally remove your crutches so you can’t confuse your success with His power.

That relationship you depended on.
That plan you idolized.
That version of control you tried to maintain.
When it falls apart, you think God abandoned you.
But He’s actually positioning you.
Because victory that comes from God looks impossible until it happens.
And when it happens… no one gets the credit but Him.
That’s where Gideon finally stepped into who God said he was.
Not because he became strong.
But because he started believing God was.
This is the part you can’t skip.
You don’t need more ability.
You need surrender.
Because the real issue was never your lack—it was your unbelief.
Hebrews 11:6 says, “Without faith it is impossible to please God…”
And faith begins where your excuses end.
But let’s go deeper—because Gideon’s story points to something greater.
Gideon was a weak man God used to deliver Israel temporarily.
Jesus Christ is the perfect Savior who delivers completely.

Gideon needed signs to believe.
Jesus became the sign.

Gideon fought with 300 men.
Jesus stood alone.

Gideon defeated an external enemy.
Jesus defeated sin, death, and hell.
“While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
That’s the Gospel.
You weren’t strong enough.
You weren’t ready.
You weren’t worthy.
But Jesus didn’t wait for you to become enough.
He became everything for you.
Through His death and resurrection, He offers what Gideon never could—true salvation.
Not just rescue from circumstances…
Rescue from sin.

That secret compromise you keep justifying.
That pride you mask as independence.
That delay in obedience you call “waiting.”
God isn’t asking you to fix yourself first.
He’s calling you to repent.
To turn.
To stop running.
To stop negotiating.
Acts 3:19 says, “Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out…”
This is your moment.
Not someday.
Not when you feel stronger.
Now.
Because the same God who told Gideon “Go in the strength you have” is looking at you—and calling you out of hiding.
But one path leads to delay, excuses, and a slow drift away from God.
The other leads to surrender, transformation, and a life that actually means something in eternity.
You already feel which one is true.
So say it.
Confess it.
Drop the excuse you’ve been hiding behind and admit where you’ve been resisting God.
And if you’re serious about walking this out—about understanding Scripture, confronting sin, and actually becoming who God is calling you to be—step into deeper discipleship here:
This isn’t about motivation.
This is about transformation.
